### The default test run runs inline again, never as a verification job, and a passed run is recorded for the push and release gates

change `pnysnkmzllot` · [log `8a758c81b7e2`](https://terminalvalue.net/raw-traces/b74acbd8-95de-40d7-8793-79948e8c27ae/8a758c81b7e2381c1664737b0b6c6c57f3e2b913ba15b4eb6af7f4e8bcfb6812.jsonl.gz)

The user decided to take the default run out of the verification pipeline: as a job it overlapped other runs in one cargo target directory (VF-034), was cut off with its runner at the Bash tool's 10-minute limit, and skipped the one-at-a-time lock when queued from a line that predated it. verification/default_tests.py (queue, step, supersede, bisect, the unread-file list, flaky counts) and its tests are removed, with verification/default-tests-unread.txt and the watcher's default-tests event.

New lib/tools/default_run.py: a whole default run (test_costs.py run) that passes records the git tree it tested, as jj snapshots the working copy, and only when no file changed during the run, in ~/.cache/in-the-loop/default-runs.jsonl. The record covers a commit of the same tree, or one differing only in traces, decisions and job records. sync.py push and release.py cut ask default_run.py gate --run, which runs the default run inline when no record covers @-; --skip-tests stays the user's alone. Every test_costs.py run holds a lock in the workspace's cargo target directory, so two runs in one workspace take turns.

Docs follow: CLAUDE.md (Verification jobs exempts the default run; Tests says inline, the record and the gate; the tests: queued brief bullet is gone), runtime.md (merges run the default run inline, the watcher's default-tests row and the release gate), the prove-java-change skill, verification/README.md, lib/README.md, llm-dlc/README.md, brief-template.md (one inline test rule replaces the Inline/Queued policy, which also settles the mismatch left by the run-brief merge), validate_example.py's docstring, and a line in VF-034.

> We will do these changes after watcher makes a push, so as not to interupt. Let's go one step further: remove the ability for verification loop to run default tests, and just have them run inline again as before. Analyze what changes will need to be made across for that to be implemented.

**Reply:**

Here's the analysis. I didn't change anything. Running the default test run as a job arrived in one burst on 2026-11-17, from `yooukqwl` (00:57) to `kzwsnszx`/`pvqrosuv` (01:59). Undoing it touches about 20 files, and three questions need your answer first.

## Decisions for you

1. **What "inline as before" means.** Before `yooukqwl`, the rule was the whole default run before every commit, and that run took about 16 minutes. Since then it has dropped to 4.6–7 minutes, because test binaries and Python files now run several at a time (`lptpzxup`).
   - **(a)** Go back to the whole run before every commit. That's about 5 minutes per commit for every loop.
   - **(b)** Keep "tests of what you changed" (`run --changed`) before each commit, and run the whole default run inline at the same points as now: when an example is done, after a merge, and before a push or release.
   - I recommend (b). The rest of this note works for either.
2. **What replaces the push and release gate.** Today `sync.py push` and `release.py cut` look for a passed *job* covering `@-`. Once there are no such jobs, the options are:
   - drop the gate, as before;
   - have `push` and `cut` run the default run inline themselves, about 5 minutes;
   - or have `test_costs.py run` write a local record of a passed run at a clean tree, and have the gate check that.
